whatItIs.text: A long, flat cut from the cow's abdominal muscle with a pronounced grain — marinated, grilled hot, and always sliced thin against the grain.

historyNote.text: The term 'flank steak' was first recorded in 1902, and the cut only became popular in North America after soldiers came home from the World Wars; in Argentina, Chile, and Brazil, where wasting nothing was tradition, flank had been a staple since the late 1700s.

howToChoose.text: Choose a deep-red steak with even fat and no browning; skirt steak is the near-identical neighbour, and butchers (and menus) mix the names freely.

storage.text: Keep raw beef sealed on the bottom shelf, away from ready-to-eat food; freeze if the date is closing in.

useItUp.text: Leftover flank is the fajita filling of tomorrow — slice it cold for sandwiches.

substitutions.note: richer, more marbled; cooks even faster
